newsitem.title: USA: El Paso to build 250 MW Brazilian plant.
newsitem.headline: El Paso to build 250 MW Brazilian plant.

text.p: El Paso Energy Corp said on Monday that it has agreed to build a $100 million, 250 megawatt power plant in Manaus, the capital city of Amazonas state in Brazil.
The first phase of construction is set to be on line by November of 1997 to alleviate frequent blackouts and power shortages in the city, El Paso Energy said in a statement.
The shortages are a result of increased electricity demand and an unusually dry period that is curtailing hydroelectric generating capacity, the company said.
El Paso said the first phase of the contract is for 44 megawatts and the remaining two phases of the project are planned to be operational in early January 1998.

Initially, the plant will use simple cycle turbine generators powered by fuel oil, but El Paso said it plans to convert the plants to natural gas-fired combined cycle plants within the next four to five years.
Power from the plants will be sold under a four-year contract to Eletronorte with an option to extend the deal another one to six years, El Paso said.
El Paso said it expects to conclude an arrangement with a partner for the project in about 30 days to finance the project at year-end start-up.
